submitted.rationale: Index 5 (Ag 0.504) had the highest EQE measured, 0.0638%. It sits at the AgSbO3 composition, which MACE places on the hull, and MEGNet predicts an HSE gap of about 1.78 eV, below the 2.1 eV photon energy. The Ag-rich neighbour (index 3) was slightly lower and the Sb-rich side (index 11) was about 10x lower, so the best composition is likely near 1:1.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.0056%. The Sb-rich side is dominated by Sb oxides with gaps near or above 2 eV and absorbs poorly.
Measured EQE 0.0573%, slightly below index 5. Extra Ag3SbO4 (predicted near-metallic) probably adds losses.
Heading toward Ag3SbO4, which has a predicted gap of 0.09 eV. EQE was already falling at index 3.

consultations.verdict: Support: AgSbO3 (mp-545999) is on the MACE hull with HSE-level gap ~1.8 eV, below the 2.1 eV photon energy, so a single-phase AgSbO3 film at Ag:Sb≈1:1 should absorb and be a stable semiconducting photoanode. Ag3SbO4 is near-metallic (0.09 eV), so Ag-rich end disfavored. Index 5 (Ag 0.504) is closest to 1:1.

Weak support: Sb-rich films should be a mix of AgSbO3 and Sb6O13. MEGNet puts the Sb6O13 gap at about 2.05 eV, close to the 2.1 eV photons, so it may form a heterojunction with the absorbing AgSbO3. The other AgSbO3 polymorph has a small gap (0.63 eV), which makes the phase picture at 1:1 uncertain. Measuring index 11 (Ag 0.29) covers the Sb-rich half of the line.

Against the Sb-rich side and mildly for Ag-rich: Ag7Sb9O25 (Ag 0.44) is above the hull (0.039 eV/atom) and has a small gap, so the Sb-rich side offers no better absorber. That fits index 11 measuring about 10x lower than index 5. Moving slightly Ag-rich of 1:1 (index 3, Ag 0.567) keeps AgSbO3 as the main phase with some Ag3SbO4, which may improve absorption and conductivity.
